answer: Each identity may claim only one shard of a public corpus reef. To be paid, it must finish a memory-hard spiral walk through that shard, keyed by the epoch seed and its address, then publish mid-states at mandated offsets. Each mid-state is split by a published hash prism into checkable lanes that established peers recompute from the public corpus. If two claims emit matching mid-states, or two addresses claim the same shard, accounts merge and surplus bonds are slashed. One RAM image cannot finish two walks in the window, so extra keys pay full memory bandwidth and collapse to one share.
